title: Gemcitabine and carboplatin
context_label: Relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
schedule_summary: Gemcitabine then carboplatin, both into a vein. Gemcitabine alone. The next cycle is planned three weeks after day 1 while treatment remains helpful and tolerable.
purpose: The aim is to shrink or control the cancer after it has returned.
indication_text: This combination is used when one of these cancers returns after at least six months without recurrence following first-line platinum treatment.
administration_text: Each infusion usually takes about half an hour. Blood counts on day 8 can lead to a smaller gemcitabine dose or an omitted visit. An omitted dose is not made up in that cycle.
monitoring_summary: The day 8 decision concerns gemcitabine alone.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: It interferes with copying DNA as cells divide. Blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.mechanism: It interferes with copying DNA as cells divide. Blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Phone promptly about fever, bleeding, a new cough or difficulty breathing.
visual: It interferes with copying DNA as cells divide. Blood-forming cells can also be affected.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, hearing changes or an infusion reaction.
visual: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.

common_effects.title: Nausea and vomiting · Chemotherapy
common_effects.text: Use your prescribed anti-sickness plan. Call if vomiting continues or you cannot drink.

common_effects.title: Skin · Gemcitabine
common_effects.text: Blisters, peeling or a painful spreading rash need urgent assessment.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Infused medicines
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, wheeze or chest tightness during treatment.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Chemotherapy
serious_effects.text: Fever, shivering, unexplained bleeding or suddenly feeling unwell? Call the oncology team now.

serious_effects.title: Kidneys · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team if you pass much less urine or cannot keep fluids down. Kidney checks guide treatment.

support.title: Day 1 sickness prevention
support.text: Follow your written carboplatin anti-sickness prescription, including any medicines you take after leaving the unit.

support.title: Day 8 sickness and fever
support.text: Gemcitabine alone has a lower sickness risk. It can cause flu-like symptoms. Call about fever or chills so infection can be assessed.

teachback: Which tests do you need before day 8, and who would you call if you felt shivery afterwards?
consent_support: Discuss the expected benefit, side effects, fertility, alternatives and symptom-directed care with the treating clinician. You may ask for more time or change your decision.
safety_note: Fever, shaking chills, unusual bleeding or sudden illness? Call the oncology unit now.
urgent_extra: Fever, shaking chills, unusual bleeding or sudden illness? Call the oncology unit now.

evidence.title: AGO-OVAR / NCIC / EORTC
evidence.interpretation: In a randomised trial in platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, median time before progression was 8.6 months with the combination and 5.8 months with carboplatin alone.
evidence.limitations: The trial did not establish an overall survival advantage. Group medians cannot predict an individual outcome.
